newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Four food contracts approved for Iraq, 113 pending.
newsitem.headline: Four food contracts approved for Iraq, 113 pending.

text.p: The United Nations said on Tuesday that funds from oil sales under the Iraqi oil-for-food plan had reached $386 million and four contracts for wheat, rice and tea had been approved.
The foodstuffs contracts, according to U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard, included:
Eckhard said $113 million had been distributed from oil proceeds and additional sums were to be dispersed this week. Oil contacts remained at 26, with none pending.
On contacts for humanitarian supplies, the Security Council's sanctions committee, which must approve contracts, considered 10 applications, blocked one and put five others on hold.

But he said the United Nations had received 131 applications from vendors selling food, medicine and other goods. He said those passed on to the sanctions committee are "determined by funds available" from oil revenues.

The "oil-for-food" agreement, which took effect Dec. 10, permits Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food, medicine and other necessities to offset the effects of sanctions imposed after Iraq's August 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Iraq's U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon, however, said that two months after the agreement became operative, no humanitarian goods had yet arrived in Iraq. He said the process of getting contracts approved by the U.N. Iraqi sanctions committee was "very cumbersome and time-consuming."
